correctness.rationale: Audited the narrowed repair and its retained formulas. Decomposing into constants, zero-mean vectors on each part, and the part-constant contrast gives exponents 0, b^2, a^2, N^2; when a=b the two zero-mean subspaces simply share an eigenvalue. Diagonal and cross-part entries cannot be negative, and the rows sum to one. For each H the derivative has exactly one change from negative to positive and the limit is positive. The strictly decreasing u(x) of the directly checked prior multipartite theorem gives tau_A<tau_B for a<b and equality when a=b. For unequal sizes the signed negative mass difference D=V-U has D(0)=0, D'(0)=b-a>0 and a negative limit. In G'=d(e^(a^2 t)D')/dt the positive-to-negative magnitude ratio is a strictly decreasing exponential. Thus G first possibly rises and then strictly falls; its positive initial value and negative limit give exactly one sign change for D'. The unique positive zero of D lies beyond tau_A because D(tau_A)=V(tau_A)>0. On (0,tau_A) this makes V>U>0, from tau_A up to tau_B only V has positive part, and at t=0 or after final recovery both row norms are one. The induced norm formula and strictness follow, with equality of row types by symmetry in the balanced case. At the unique minimum of H_B, the ratio of its exponentials is exp(-(N^2-a^2)*theta_B)=a/N, giving the claimed peak time and value. The sign extremizer is correct by equality in the absolute row sum and also works on complex input. An independent small direct matrix replay checked balanced, moderately unbalanced and more unbalanced pairs. Corrections do not alter the original support script or its frozen record.
residual_risks: The replay is finite numerical corroboration only. The comparison concerns unweighted bicliques with both parts of size at least two, not arbitrary multipartite graphs or Laplacian powers.

originality.rationale: This PASS is for the repaired statement only, not the original package presented as a new exact recovery and scale result. The earlier multipartite record mechanically covers the full positivity horizon, ordered within-part cutoffs, both recovery scales (by its proof of the endpoint limits of u), and the norm as a maximum over two explicit terms. A distinct same-day result already gives the same exact unique peak for b>=32a and three of the four frozen scale limits, more generally as b/a tends to infinity. The repair makes these overlaps explicit, removes the misdescription of the linked three-level semigroup example, and narrows the contribution to strict larger-row dominance at every transient time for all size ratios, including the consequent resolved all-ratio peak. The intrinsic sign comparison is not supplied by a maximum formula or by the earlier large-imbalance peak comparison. No priority is inferred within the shared date.
residual_risks: No within-day order is established. Bounded primary search found no additional exact match, not proof of historical priority. Gazzola–Grunau full text was not retrievable; the comparison is limited to its open scope.

value.rationale: The repaired comparison identifies, at every time and without a size-ratio hypothesis, which vertex class controls worst-case coordinatewise amplification and hence where to construct the maximizing sign input. It converts a two-candidate temporal optimization into one explicit unique peak for all bicliques. This is a structural answer not contained in the known positivity scales or generic maximum formulas.
residual_risks: No broader conclusion is made about competition among parts in a general complete multipartite graph. The known recovery limits are context, not independent added value.
